The dust has settled, the turf is down, and the gates have officially opened. Carhartt, America's premium workwear brand, has once again partnered with the Buffalo Bills as they prepare to kick off their next era at the newly completed Highmark Stadium. To mark the occasion, Carhartt is shining a spotlight on the hardworking people behind-the-scenes who built the new Buffalo stage, as well as the tradespeople nationwide who supply the game's essential elements. This work comes together in the next chapter of Carhartt's creative brand campaign, Made Possible, which honors the tradespeople whose hard work shapes some of our beloved and iconic shared experiences.

In the first chapter of the Made Possible campaign, which launched in August 2025, Carhartt highlighted the early stages of Highmark Stadium's construction through the story of Bills legendary running back Thurman Thomas and his commercial construction company, 34 Group Inc., which was responsible for installing the seats in the new stadium. This fall, the campaign picks up where that story left off, with Thurman showcasing the dedication, craftsmanship and pride of his crew and the thousands of hardworking people who helped bring the stadium to life by giving current Bills star running back James Cook III his first tour of the state-of-the-art venue.

"Stadiums aren't just concrete and steel, they are monuments to what can happen when grit, skill, and purpose come together," said Norma Delaney, Vice President of Marketing and Brand Creative at Carhartt. "This season, we are proud to stand alongside Bills legend and construction leader Thurman Thomas, and current Bills running back James Cook III to honor the hardworking crews whose contributions are often overlooked but are critical to every game-day experience. From the first shovel in the ground to the opening kickoff, major construction projects like the new Highmark Stadium are made possible by hardworking people wearing Carhartt."

The campaign is anchored by a 30-second hero spot, "Making Football Possible," which is a unique, reverse-look from finish to start, beginning with the fans cheering, rewinding to the seats being installed, the sod being rolled, the uprights going in, and the footballs being created, because it takes a collective effort of hardworking skilled tradespeople to make game day possible. While the campaign is anchored in Buffalo, this fall's installment expands its lens to celebrate the workforce behind stadiums nationwide that support football year-round – from the sod to the uprights.

The campaign also includes two-minute longform, behind-the-scenes videos:
• Constructing Highmark Stadium alongside Thurman Thomas and his crew at 34 Group Inc.
• Carolina Green, the family-owned farm serving as one of the major natural grass suppliers for NFL stadiums across the country.
• Aluminum Athletic Equipment (AAE) and the skilled welders behind the uprights that define the end zone in multiple NFL stadiums.

This multi-year campaign celebrates the physical completion of Highmark Stadium while honoring the grit of the thousands of men and women who bring the game to life.

"It's an honor to take the field in this new stadium, but we know none of this happens without the crews who actually built the stage we play on," said James Cook III, Buffalo Bills Running Back. "Partnering with Carhartt and Thurman to officially pass the torch and thank the workers behind the scenes is the perfect way to kick off this exciting new chapter for Bills fans."

Additionally, when the Bills take the Highmark Stadium field for their first preseason home game on Saturday, Aug. 15, Carhartt will thank the hardworking people who brought the new stadium to life with a Rally Towel giveaway for the first 20,000 fans in attendance. The Rally Towels will be printed on the front and back and will feature the names of every person on the crews who worked on the new stadium. Carhartt will also run messaging in-stadium during the Bills preseason games to pay tribute to the crews.

PepsiCo® continues to expand its snack portfolio in Mexico with the launch of PopCorners®, a product designed to redefine one of the category's most familiar formats. Featuring a distinctive triangular shape, a unique texture and a bold personality, PopCorners® invites consumers to experience popcorn in an entirely new way.
For decades, popcorn seemed to have reached its final form. PopCorners® challenges that assumption by proving that even the most established products can evolve. Its signature triangular shape breaks category conventions while becoming the symbol of a new snacking experience created for consumers looking for products that deliver both enjoyment and fun.
The launch is driven not only by product innovation but also by changing consumer expectations. PopCorners® was created for people who enjoy discovering brands with personality, originality and a fresh perspective. The idea is simple: changing the shape can also change the experience, transforming an everyday snack into something completely unexpected.
That insight became the foundation of the brand's launch campaign, developed together with independent creative agency Zurda México. The campaign turns the product's unconventional shape into the center of the conversation, introducing PopCorners® as a playful, irreverent and approachable brand.
Creatively, the campaign uses the triangular shape as its strongest brand asset, placing it across different worlds and characters to reinforce one simple idea: when a category evolves, the way we talk about it should evolve too.
"You can't launch a triangular product with a square campaign. That's why we brought in cavemen, Egyptians, superheroes and even an astronaut," said Jorge Cordero and Rubén Cabezas, Creative Directors at Zurda México.
As part of the project, Zurda México developed the brand strategy, positioning, creative platform, visual identity and a comprehensive content ecosystem to support PopCorners®' launch in the Mexican market.
"At PopCorners, we believe that even the most familiar products can be reinvented. We're arriving in Mexico to challenge the idea that popcorn always has to be round and to show that a different shape can also deliver a completely new texture and flavor experience. This launch reflects PepsiCo's ongoing commitment to innovation and to expanding its portfolio with products that respond to evolving consumer preferences. With PopCorners, we want to connect with people looking for something different, surprising and full of personality, because innovation also means challenging what we've always taken for granted," said Juan Cuevas, Marketing Director for PopCorners Mexico.
With the arrival of PopCorners®, PepsiCo® continues to strengthen its snack portfolio with products designed to meet evolving consumer preferences while reinforcing its commitment to innovation across the category. PopCorners® enters the Mexican market with a proposition that combines a distinctive identity, a different snacking experience and a campaign that invites consumers to rethink everything they thought they knew about popcorn.

In May 2026, three of France’s most influential content creators — Squeezie, Inoxtag and Léna Situations — unveiled an unexpected collaboration: not a content project or a one-off partnership, but a new energy drink brand, Ciao Energy. The launch brought together three complementary personalities and their combined communities of several tens of millions of followers, turning creator influence into a fully-fledged consumer brand.

Ciao Energy is positioned as a less sugary and more transparent alternative to traditional energy drinks, with six original flavors including White Peach, Apricot Raspberry, Kiwi Cucumber and Double Lychee. The brand builds on Squeezie’s existing Ciao universe, launched with Ciao Kombucha in 2025, while giving Inoxtag and Léna Situations an equal role as co-founders rather than simply endorsing the product.

The collaboration also carries a strong personal dimension. Inoxtag had been working for several years on his own energy drink project, Gang Potion, but struggled to bring it to market. With the support and expertise of Squeezie and Léna Situations, the idea was finally transformed into Ciao Energy — with Double Lychee becoming the flavor associated with Inoxtag.

Beyond the product itself, Ciao Energy illustrates a broader shift in the creator economy: creators are no longer simply media channels for brands. They are increasingly becoming entrepreneurs, co-founders and brand builders, bringing together audience, cultural relevance and product development. Ciao Energy is a particularly strong example of this evolution, combining three major creator profiles around a shared brand vision rather than a traditional influencer partnership.

Confused.com and Leo UK are bringing some of the nation’s most familiar sayings to life in a new campaign capturing the disproportionately good feeling of having Just Used Confused.com.

‘Feels like…’ is the latest chapter of the award-winning brand platform, which celebrates the fleeting sense of triumph that comes from conquering life admin, saving some money and feeling, briefly, like a fully functioning adult. The 2025 instalment of the platform won multiple Golds at Creative Circle and British Arrows, including the prestigious John Webster Award.

Each film begins in the real world as someone finishes sorting their insurance with Confused.com. Their relief triggers a comedic cutaway into a heightened world where the feeling is expressed through a familiar idiom, interpreted very literally by a cast of handcrafted animal puppets. The environments and supporting characters were developed and enhanced with AI production tools.

In ‘The Cat That Got the Cream’, a man sorting his car insurance cuts to an ageing, bespectacled cat in a supermarket. After seriously considering whether he deserves a pot of cream, the cat drops it into his basket and reasons: “Cream, double cream! That’s coming home with me that, Meow.”

‘Laughing ’til the Cow Comes Home’ introduces Pig and Sheep, two laid-back former university housemates enjoying an afternoon of doing very little while Cow is at his nine-to-five. Pig is midway through a joke when Cow appears in the doorway, briefcase in hand, and shouts: “Oh please don’t stop on my account...”

Completing the trio is ‘The Early Bird That Got the Worm’, starring a polished and profoundly pleased-with-herself blue tit. Carrying a shopping bag emblazoned with a worm, she struts past a queue of less fortunate birds and announces: “you should’ve set your alarms”.

The characters were developed with BlinkInk stop motion directing duo, Andy Biddle and Adeena Grubb, with every detail designed to build their personalities, from the cat’s increasingly necessary reading glasses to Cow’s carefully pressed workwear, and the early bird’s jumper draped deliberately over her shoulders. 

Biddle was a lead animator on Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs, while Grubb is a multi-award-winning puppet maker and animation director. Their combined experience in handcrafted filmmaking helped bring the campaign’s familiar idioms to life through characters packed with charm, wit and sharply observed detail. 

Each film ends with the line, “Insurance feels better when you’ve just used Confused.com”, followed by the familiar Confused.com whistle, performed by its respective puppet character. First introduced with the launch of the ‘Just Used Confused.com’ platform, the whistle has since grown into an established sonic asset for the brand.

The campaign will be supported by ten and six second edits, alongside radio and social activity, and will run across TV, BVOD, social and radio in the UK from 7th August. 

The campaign was developed with Zenith, which led media planning and buying. Together, the team delivered an integrated campaign with an effective media mix, designed to elevate the Just Use Confused.com platform and build fame nationwide.

It’s almost impossible to pick a favourite, but Angry Cow has to take the top spot. He was inspired by Mark from Peep Show, while the pig took plenty of cues from Jeremy. We even snuck in Mark’s iconic creamy elephant sofa and named the characters Mark Cowigan, Jeremy UsPork and Super Lamb. If you’re familiar with Peep Show, you’ll understand why. If you’re not… go and watch Peep Show.

The Heat Can't Beat Us 

How Midea Found a Different Way to Tell an Iraqi Story 

When people think about advertising air conditioners, the formula is almost written for you. 

Show the heat. 

Show people struggling. 

Introduce the product. 

Everyone feels better. 

It's a formula we've all seen before, and honestly, we could have followed it too. But as we started talking about Midea's summer campaign, something didn't sit right with us. 

Yes, Iraq is incredibly hot. During the summer, temperatures climb well above 50°C, and air conditioning isn't a luxury, it's something people genuinely rely on every day. But when we thought about our own experiences of summer, and the people around us, we realized the heat wasn't the whole story. 

Life doesn't pause because it's hot. 

People still go to work. Markets are still crowded. Street vendors still prepare drinks for long lines of customers. Families still go shopping together. Friends still meet by the river. Kids still find ways to cool off. 

Summer wasn't something Iraqis were trying to escape. 

It was something they had learned to live with. 

That realization became the starting point for everything that followed. 

Instead of asking ourselves how we could make another air conditioner commercial, we started asking a different question. 

What does summer actually feel like when you live in Iraq? 

For a while, we stopped thinking about the product altogether. Instead, we started paying attention. 

The more we looked around, the more we noticed the little moments we normally take for granted. 

The sound of ice being crushed into a glass of shanina. 

A juice vendor pouring another drink before the previous customer had even walked away. 

A watermelon being sliced open at a market. 

The mist of water spraying over people trying to cool down. 

The familiar buzz of traffic on a hot afternoon. 

A scooter carrying giant blocks of ice through the city. 

An old man sitting outside with a cup of hot tea, completely comfortable despite the temperature. 

A family walking through the front door after grocery shopping, immediately relaxing the moment the cool air reaches them. 

Individually, these moments don't seem particularly remarkable. Together, they tell you exactly where you are. They're the little details every Iraqi knows without ever really thinking about them. 

At some point during those conversations, someone said something that changed the whole direction of the campaign. 

“What if summer isn't just something you see?” 

Summer has its own soundtrack. You hear it before you even notice it. 

That single idea became the film. The crack of ice. The splash of water. The rustle of clothes catching cool air. The hum of an air conditioner quietly filling a room. Every location had its own note, and together they became one continuous piece of music—which is how Symphony of Summer found its name. 

One of my favorite parts of this project wasn't even in the final edit. It was being out in Baghdad while we were filming. 

Because we weren't shooting on closed sets or isolated locations, people naturally became curious. They stopped to watch. 

A lot of them wanted to know why we were paying so much attention to details most people walk past without a second glance, why a crew would spend that long filming ice being crushed into a glass, or a vendor pouring juice. The scale of it made people assume this had to be something bigger than a single campaign. More than a few were convinced we were shooting an entire series. 

Others simply smiled and stayed for a few minutes before continuing with their day. 

There was something special about that. We weren't creating an artificial version of Iraqi summer. We were standing right in the middle of it. 

Looking back, those interactions reminded us why authenticity mattered so much for this campaign. If the people living these moments recognized themselves in what we were filming, we knew we were heading in the right direction. 

When the film was finally finished, we realized it wasn't really about air conditioning. 

It was about recognition. 

It was about seeing familiar moments on screen and thinking, “That's us.” 

The product still had an important role to play, but it didn't need to dominate every frame. It simply became part of a story that already existed. 

I think that's what made Symphony of Summer different. 

We didn't begin with a script. 

We didn't begin with the product. 

We began by observing. By listening. 

By paying attention to the sounds, routines, and little rituals that make an Iraqi summer feel uniquely Iraqi. 

Because in the end, no product wins a real place in someone's home. It has to earn a place in their story first and this summer, ours got to sound like Iraq.

Throughout the year, in advertising, the “blank canvas” is synonymous with briefings, tight deadlines, and the constant search for ideas. A process that sometimes brings a harvest, and other times leaves behind deep exhaustion.

But in summer, the rules change. The blank canvas is no longer a challenge waiting for us to fill it quickly; it becomes the sea, the breeze, and the sun. It is the canvas itself that comes to free us from the weight of the year.

That is why, from La Caseta, we want to share our summer campaign with you: a modern Spanish Romance transformed into a song. A tribute to the need to pause, in order to find inspiration again.
La Caseta has created A Spanish Romance of the Blank Canvas as a metaphor for what it means to take on every briefing throughout the year, and what this blank canvas represents during the summer.
A deeply poetic campaign, both visually and conceptually, for which a poem has been created: a modern Spanish Romance of the blank canvas transformed into a song. The decision to create a modern Spanish romance in the form of a song comes from the role this poetic form has played in Spanish literature for centuries: a way of sharing stories, emotions, and collective memory. The romance brought poetry closer to people because its simple language and musical rhythm allowed anyone to hear it, learn it, and sing it. That is why, when speaking about something so universal within our industry, we felt it was the form that best represented the beauty, simplicity, and importance of what a blank canvas means during the summer.

In our profession, everything must be creative, impactful, and different. That is why it is often said that every time we are asked to create a campaign and begin a project from scratch, we are facing a blank canvas. And although we also encounter this blank canvas during the summer, when we step away from our work and allow ourselves to disconnect, it takes on a completely different meaning: we are no longer the ones filling the blank canvas; instead, it is the canvas that fills us with energy and frees us from the stress, exhaustion, and demanding deadlines we have carried throughout the rest of the year.

All of this can be seen throughout the poem. That is why, this summer, all of us who work in advertising and communication will continue creating and facing blank canvases with every campaign while we are in the office. But when we step outside, travel, or go on holiday, we will recharge and find inspiration in all the blank canvases we encounter: a window, the sea, a meal, the sun…
Because for us, summer is also a vast blank canvas of inspiring experiences, of things waiting to be felt and lived.

Rice Krispies Treats expands its “Treat Your Inner Child” campaign with a new pair of spots directed by Voyager’s Grayson Whitehurst, leaning further into a playful, escapist world that blurs the line between everyday routine and imagination.    

Created as a second installment of the campaign introduced in 2025, the new work builds on the idea that a Rice Krispies Treats bar can spark a small break from routine, unlocking a more spontaneous, carefree state of mind. The product serves as the entry point into each surreal world, inspiring environments built from its ingredients, textures and playful spirit.  

Each spot begins in a familiar, more serious setting before quickly shifting into a surreal fantasy. In one, a man stuck on hold at his desk takes a bite of a Rice Krispies Treats bar and is transported into a world made entirely of its ingredients, ziplining through towering crispy rice and marshmallow mountains alongside animated goats that spring to life mid-yodel. In another, a routine elevator ride transforms into a marshmallow-filled world, where a woman floats and bounces through massive, cloud-like forms after tasting a Rice Krispies Treats Homestyle bar, subtly highlighting the product’s larger size in comparison to the brand's core offering.  

The spots move quickly from ordinary routines into surreal fantasy environments, balancing large-scale visual worlds with grounded performances and tactile production design. Shot in Romania alongside BBDO and local production partners, the campaign was built to deliver cinematic transitions within condensed 15- and 6-second formats.

“We wanted each spot to capture that private moment when routine breaks and joy feels easy again,” shares Grayson. “The fantasy was a physical expression of that feeling. So, we approached everything as tangible and real: practical builds, sculpted textures, grounded performances, with VFX used to expand the world rather than replace it. Because the spots had to work in 15s and 6s, every choice was about entering imagination quickly while still letting the release breathe and giving the humor of each moment room to land.”

Each spot closes with the tagline, “Treat Your Inner Child.”

When Ecuador faced Argentina in the South American Qualifiers, the biggest advantage wasn't on the pitch.

Naldo, an Argentine retailer, was the official sponsor of the Argentina National Team, with the rights to use the image of Lionel Messi, Emiliano "Dibu" Martínez, Lautaro Martínez and the rest of the world champions.

La Ganga had none of that.

So instead of competing with sponsorship money, it competed with creativity.

A few days before the match, La Ganga publicly challenged Naldo with a simple bet: if Ecuador won, Naldo would lend La Ganga the image rights of Argentina's players for one social media post. If Argentina won, La Ganga would publicly recognize Naldo as the winner.

The challenge quickly spread across social media, sports media and news outlets, turning a football match into a brand rivalry that fans wanted to follow.

Against all odds, Ecuador defeated Argentina.

Naldo honored the bet.

Within hours, La Ganga published a campaign featuring Messi, Lautaro Martínez, Emiliano Martínez and the reigning world champions—without paying a single dollar for their image rights.

What would normally require one of the most expensive sponsorship deals in football became the result of one bold creative idea.

The campaign generated nationwide conversation, earned extensive media coverage, sparked thousands of organic interactions and proved that, sometimes, the smartest way to compete against a sponsorship isn't buying one—it's making people talk about yours.
